{{Quote|But you know that all that is Kesh came from the ''Skyborn''. Nothing can be born of Kesh anew!|Izri Dazh, to Adari Vaal|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
In the [[Keshiri religion]], the '''Skyborn''' were the group of deities worshiped by the lords of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. The [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] believed that in mythic [[Time/Legends|times]] the Skyborn [[Great Battle|battled]] the evil [[Otherside]] in the [[Star/Legends|stars]] above Kesh. The Skyborn were victorious, but the [[Blood/Legends|blood]] from their wounds fell upon Kesh's seas and formed all of the world's landmass. Subsequently, the Skyborn were said to watch over the planet, which was ruled by the supposed "Sons of the Skyborn," the [[Neshtovar]]. In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], a group of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] led by [[Yaru Korsin]] crash-landed on Kesh, and were found in the [[Takara Mountains|Cetajan Mountains]] by Keshiri [[Geology|geologist]] [[Adari Vaal]]. Subsequently, the Sith claimed to be the Skyborn returned to Kesh, and took full advantage of the fanatical devotion of the Keshiri masses. Once they were in control, the Sith changed the name of the Skyborn to the '''Protectors''', de-emphasizing the tales of the Skyborn and the Otherside in favor of older myths. In the new belief system of the Keshiri religion, the Protectors battled the [[Destructors]] over the course of history, always guarding Kesh from their enemies' violent purposes. Eventually, the Sith came to accept that they truly were the Protectors and continued to be worshiped by the Keshiri for millennia.

==Mythology==
{{Quote|This land was a part of the living Skyborn. Do you think they do not hear you? When the ground quakes, when the smokers burn&mdash;it's their remnant acting in sympathy with their wishes. Their wishes that we honor them, and hate the Otherside!|Izri Dazh, to Adari Vaal|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
The Skyborn were a group of deities widely worshiped on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]], as early as the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]]. The [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] natives of the planet exalted the Skyborn as "the great beings above," and the Skyborn were the basis of the story of Kesh's creation. It was believed that many [[Time/Legends|ages]] past, the [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] Skyborn, riding colossal [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] [[uvak]] beasts, battled the nefarious [[Otherside]] in the [[Star/Legends|stars]]. The [[Great Battle]], as it was called, raged for eons, and although the Skyborn were injured, they eventually defeated the Otherside. As a result of their wounds, drops of Skyborn [[Blood/Legends|blood]] fell upon the [[Water/Legends|seas]] of Kesh, creating all of the planet's land&mdash;a belief supported in a way by the highly asymmetrical Keshiri coastlines.<ref name="skyborn" />

The Skyborn were seen as all-knowing. [[Geology|Geological]] events such as [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquakes]] and [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic]] eruptions were believed to be the remnant of the Skyborn acting according to their wishes that the Keshiri honor them and hate the Otherside. If one was seen as having disgraced the Skyborn, it was commonly believed that the gods would "forsake" them, bringing punishment upon the erring individual. Conversely, one could also be protected by the Skyborn, who would prevent harm from coming to that person.<ref name="skyborn" /> After the arrival on Kesh of a group of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] claiming to be the legendary Skyborn in 5000 BBY, the Skyborn myth was changed somewhat. The names of the Skyborn and the Otherside were changed to the Protectors and the [[Destructors]], respectively, harkening back to earlier Keshiri tales&mdash;the Destructors were said to periodically come to Kesh to bring destruction to the planet, while the Protectors were destined to defeat them.<ref name="paragon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref> This idea was given some credence due to evidence that a planetwide catastrophe like the one that the Destructors were said to bring had been visited upon the world at least once. The Keshiri looked to the Protectors to defend Kesh from the Destructors' eventual return.<ref name="omen" />

==History==
{{Quote|We are the Skyborn&mdash;and we ''will'' return to the stars!|Yaru Korsin|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
[[File:Lost_Sith_Tribe_world.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The mountainous landscape of Kesh, said to have been created by the Skyborn]]
By 5000 BBY, the worship of the Skyborn was firmly entrenched as a dominant force in daily Keshiri life. Tradition held that in past ages the uvak-riding group known as the [[Neshtovar]] brought the knowledge of the Skyborn and the Great Battle from Kesh's [[Takara Mountains|Cetajan Mountains]]. The Neshtovar were proclaimed as the "Sons of the Skyborn," and took authority as the rulers of Kesh. In 5000 BBY, geologist [[Adari Vaal]] discovered evidence that the land of Kesh was created naturally from [[Magma/Legends|magma]] flow, rather than from the blood of the Skyborn as was commonly believed. After teaching her theories to students, she was called to testify before the Neshtovar and defend her supposed "heresy." As Vaal argued with Neshtovar leader [[Izri Dazh]], a sudden explosion rocked the Cetajan Mountains&mdash;the Keshiri masses took it as a sign of the Skyborn's displeasure. After being harassed by [[Tahv]] townsfolk, Vaal fled into the mountain range on an uvak. There, she came across the source of the event, a group of crash-landed [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Vaal brought the Sith to civilization, where they proclaimed themselves to be the Skyborn of legend. Although some were initially skeptical, Sith leader [[Yaru Korsin]] dismissed those doubts with [[The Force/Legends|Force]] feats, such as levitating Izri Dazh. With a lavish ceremony in Tahv's [[Circle Eternal]], the supposed Skyborn were welcomed back to Kesh and embraced their role as gods, hoping to use their newfound authority to find a way offplanet. However, as they would find, the planet Kesh did not have the materials that the Sith needed to get off the world.<ref name="skyborn" />

The Skyborn went on to marginalize the Neshtovar, moving into their homes and taking away their power. In addition, Adari Vaal, once an outcast, was honored as the "Daughter of the Skyborn."<ref name="skyborn" /> Service of the supposed Skyborn became the dominant facet of Keshiri life&mdash;many priests, such as [[Tilden Kaah]], served as little more than personal servants to their gods. The Sith gladly welcomed this sort of devotion, and looked to extend their hegemony over the Keshiri natives even more. While the Neshtovar claimed a sort of kinship to the Skyborn, no Keshiri could claim a relation to the ancient mythic Protectors, tales of whom had been overlaid by the newer [[Keshiri religion]]. The Sith ended the use of the term "Skyborn" in favor of Protectors, and the common religious beliefs were altered somewhat.<ref name="paragon" /> This change did nothing to affect the Keshiri's fanatical devotion to their gods, and many Keshiri lives were lost at hard labor, building monuments and tributes to honor the Skyborn. One of the dead was Adari Vaal's son, [[Finn Vaal|Finn]], leading her to head an ultimately-unsuccessful [[Keshiri resistance]] movement. The name "Skyborn" lived on in the [[Skyborn Rangers]], a group of ceremonial uvak-riders led by Yaru Korsin's daughter, [[Nida Korsin]]. By [[4975 BBY]], the supposed Protectors had given up on their efforts to find a way off Kesh and signaled to the masses that they would live among the Keshiri for good.<ref name="savior">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior]]''</ref>

The Sith, organized into their own [[Lost Tribe of Sith|tribe]], were worshiped as gods for millennia, with the Keshiri none the wiser. In [[3000 BBY]], a recording was discovered revealing Korsin and his group to be servants of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], which had the ability to shatter the Sith illusion.<ref name="pantheon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon]]''</ref> However, the knowledge did not make it to the Keshiri public.<ref name="secrets">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Secrets]]''</ref> In [[2975 BBY]], the Lost Tribe was also able to use the "Skyborn myth" to conquer the continent of [[Alanciar]] with minimal resistance. For millennia, the Keshiri on Alanciar had been separated from their counterparts on Keshtah Minor by a wide ocean. However, they also shared the same Skyborn legend. [[Grand Lord]] [[Varner Hilts]] was able to win the support of the Keshiri on Alanciari by using the Alanciari man [[Jogan Halder]] to convince his people that Hilt's forces were the Skyborn and that Lord [[Korsin Bentado|Bentado]], a rival Sith Lord, was a servant of the evil Destructors. Thus, the Sith were able to consolidate control of Alanciar with minimal blood spilled and disruption.<ref name="pandemonium">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pandemonium]]''</ref>

However, some Alanciari Sith like [[Quarra Thayn]] and [[Chegg]] realized that the Lost Tribe were not gods but were actually mere mortal beings.<ref name="pandemonium" /><ref name="Spiral 1">[[Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral 1|''Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral'' 1]]</ref> During an expedition to the frozen continent of [[Eshkrene]], the Human Sith [[Parlan Spinner]] and [[Takara Hilts]] encountered [[the Doomed]], the multi-species descendants of ancient [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] who had discovered Kesh following the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] which ended in [[6900 BBY]]. They discovered that the Keshiri legends of the Protectors and Destructors, and the [[Great Calamity]] were based on Keshiri recollections of that conflict between the Jedi and Dark Jedi. In the end, the two rival Force orders made peace after the Dark Jedi overthrew and imprisoned their leader [[Remulus Dreypa]] within an [[Oubliette (stasis casket)|oubliette]].<ref name="Spiral 2" />

The Jedi and Dark Jedi then migrated to Eshkrene where they created a new community known as the Doomed, who were ashamed of their [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] and the destruction they had wrought on the Keshiri. They dedicated themselves to protecting the Keshiri and striving to find a balance between the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark sides]] of the Force. The Sith expedition to [[Eshkrene]] in [[2974 BBY]] ended the Doomed's isolation from the rest of Kesh. However, Spinner freed Dreypa from his prison, intending to use the Dark Jedi to settle scores with the Tribe, and escaped back to Keshtah Minor.<ref name="Spiral 2" /> Dreypa intended to return to the stars and reluctantly agreed to stage a rebellion against the Tribe as a means of reaching the Sith capital of [[Tahv]], where an ancient hyperspace-capable [[Last Hope (Jedi starship)|Jedi starship]] was hidden.<ref name="Spiral 4">[[Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral 4|''Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral'' 4]]</ref> Ultimately, Dreypa was defeated through the combined efforts of Spinner and Hilts but all members of the Doomed perished during the conflict.<ref name="Spiral 5">[[Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral 5|''Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral'' 5]]</ref>

Following the suppression of [[Dreypa's rebellion]], Lord Hilts surmised that the Keshiri's relative quick acceptance of Yaru Korsin and the Sith crew of the ''[[Omen]]'' had been no mistake since his Sith ancestors had not been the first to arrive on Kesh. He also realized that if the mythical Protectors and Destructors still existed, the Tribe would be no match for their powers.<ref name="Spiral 5" /> Over time, the Sith uncovered more evidence that the tale of the Protectors was actually true, and accepted that they truly were the figures of legend.<ref name="abyss">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Skyborn were first mentioned in [[Christie Golden]]'s [[2009]] novel ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''&mdash;the second book in the nine-part [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series&mdash;where they were called the Protectors.<ref name="omen" /> The name "Skyborn" was first introduced in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[eBook]] ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]'', along with much of their history and backstory.<ref name="skyborn" /> The deities were also mentioned in several other entries in the ''Fate of the Jedi'' and [[Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith|''Lost Tribe of the Sith'']] series, respectively.

During an email exchange dating back to [[August]] [[2013]], Miller clarified that the Skyborn actually referred to the ancient [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who had fought the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Remulus Dreypa]] and his [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] allies during the [[Great Calamity]] which occurred at an unknown period following the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]. This event later evolved into the Neshtovari legends of the Skyborn and the Otherside. Later, the Lost Tribe of Sith imposed the names Protectors and Destructors on the Skyborn and Otherside respectively. By the time of the [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] novel series, which occurs about three thousand years following the events of the [[Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral|''Spiral'']] comics, later residents on Kesh attempted to fit the Force entity [[Abeloth]] into the earlier Keshiri mythology. Miller also theorized that two cycles of destruction may have occurred on Kesh: Dreypa's [[Great Calamity|first]] and [[Dreypa's rebellion|second attacks]] overlapping and Abeloth's actions co-mingled in people's minds.<ref name="Mail">{{EmailCite|email=File:Miller response August 29 2013.jpg|creator=[[John Jackson Miller]]|date=2013-08-29}}</ref>
